newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power firms; deferreds sag.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power firms; deferreds sag.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic for Monday delivery firmed amid forecast of well-above normal temperatures this weekend along the coastal area.
"Weather is a little unsure for Monday," said an East Coast marketer.
Saturday reading for the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Inteconnect district was projected to hit the 50-60 Fahrenheit degree range during the day and 30-40 at night.
The unseasonably mild weather also pressured natural gas prices lower with weekend deliveries to the Philadelphia city gate at $3.61-$3.68 per million British thermal units.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures were last down 34.4 cents at $3.040/mmBtu.
Forward PJM prices fell today in tandem with weaker gas futures and cash values, brokers and marketers said.
Brokers and marketers noted a number of transactions for multi-day deliveries changed hands so players could lock in profits in this falling market.
Monday electricity for firm, peak PJM delivery were last assessed at $19.00-$20.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) with deals heard done in a $17.50-$20.00 range.
Today's quote was higher than Thursday's $17.50-$18.50 range for Friday.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Monday delivery climbed to steady at $15.00-$15.50, up from Thursday's $14.00-$15.00.
January 1997 PJM electricity with similar delivery terms were discussed near $28.75, down from $30.20-$30.50 Thursday.
PJM power deliveries for January and February slipped to $28.75-$29.75, down from Thursday's $29.75-$30.00.
March PJM electricity fell 25 cents to $24.75-$25.00 from Thursday's $25.00-$25.25.
First-quarter PJM deliveries were notationally pegged at $27.50-$28.00 from Thursday's $28.30-$28.50.

Other PJM deferred quotes were unchanged from Thursday's levels. Second-quarter PJM power was still assessed at $23.20-$23.40, July/August PJM $31.70-$31.90, third-quarter $29.00-$29.25, fourth-quarter 1997 $24.00-$24.50 and calendar 1997 for peak hour delivery $26.40-$26.70.
PECO Energy said its 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick unit 2 will hold at 88 percent power ahead of its refueling outage scheduled to begin January 31.
